content:
Hi. Recently, I got linker(?) errors when building Lean 4 from sources. I'd appreciate any help!

Environments

I'm using GCC 13.3.0 in an Ubuntu-derived distro. I followed the standard Lean dev setup and was able to build it a few months ago.

pandaman@pop-os:~/lean4$ cc --version
cc (Ubuntu 13.3.0-6ubuntu2~24.04.1) 13.3.0
Copyright (C) 2023 Free Software Foundation, Inc.
This is free software; see the source for copying conditions.  There is NO
warranty; not even for MERCHANTABILITY or FITNESS FOR A PARTICULAR PURPOSE.

Errors

Here is the very first error logs I encountered. I got the same error for many .c files after this.

[100%] Linking CXX static library lib/temp/libleancpp_1.a
[100%] Linking CXX static library lib/lean/libleancpp.a
⣯ [2/4777] Running Init.Prelude (+ 0 more)make[5]: Leaving directory '/home/pandaman/lean4/build/dev/stage1'
make[5]: Leaving directory '/home/pandaman/lean4/build/dev/stage1'
[100%] Built target leancpp_1
[100%] Built target leancpp
✖ [5/4777] Building Lean.Runtime:c.o
trace: .> /usr/bin/cc -c -o /home/pandaman/lean4/build/dev/stage1/lib/temp/Lean/Runtime.c.o.export /home/pandaman/lean4/build/dev/stage1/lib/temp/Lean/Runtime.c -I /home/pandaman/lean4/build/dev/stage1/include -fstack-clash-protection -fdata-sections -ffunction-sections -fPIC -fvisibility=hidden -Wno-unused-command-line-argument -O3 -DNDEBUG  -DLEAN_EXPORTING
info: stderr:
cc: warning: : linker input file unused because linking not done
cc: error: : linker input file not found: No such file or directory
error: external command '/usr/bin/cc' exited with code 1
✖ [7/4777] Building Lean.Server.Test.Refs:c.o
trace: .> /usr/bin/cc -c -o /home/pandaman/lean4/build/dev/stage1/lib/temp/Lean/Server/Test/Refs.c.o.export /home/pandaman/lean4/build/dev/stage1/lib/temp/Lean/Server/Test/Refs.c -I /home/pandaman/lean4/build/dev/stage1/include -fstack-clash-protection -fdata-sections -ffunction-sections -fPIC -fvisibility=hidden -Wno-unused-command-line-argument -O3 -DNDEBUG  -DLEAN_EXPORTING
info: stderr:
cc: warning: : linker input file unused because linking not done
cc: error: : linker input file not found: No such file or directory
error: external command '/usr/bin/cc' exited with code 1
✖ [12/4777] Building Init.MethodSpecsSimp:c.o

Cursor's Composer suggested that moreLeancArgs = [""] confuses GCC, and the following patch allowed lean4 to build. Is it something worth upstreaming? Thanks!

diff --git a/src/CMakeLists.txt b/src/CMakeLists.txt
index b764dc260e..13d6a7512b 100644
--- a/src/CMakeLists.txt
+++ b/src/CMakeLists.txt
@@ -1064,10 +1064,14 @@ configure_file(${LEAN_SOURCE_DIR}/stdlib.make.in ${CMAKE_BINARY_DIR}/stdlib.make

 # hacky
 function(toml_escape IN OUTVAR)
-  if(IN)
-    string(STRIP "${IN}" OUT)
+  string(STRIP "${IN}" OUT)
+  if(OUT)
     string(REPLACE " " "\", \"" OUT "${OUT}")
     set(${OUTVAR} "\"${OUT}\"" PARENT_SCOPE)
+  else()
+    # Avoid `moreLeancArgs = [""]` when `IN` is only whitespace: GCC then gets an empty argv
+    # token and fails with `cc: error: : linker input file not found`.
+    set(${OUTVAR} "" PARENT_SCOPE)
   endif()
 endfunction()
 string(REPLACE "ROOT" "${CMAKE_BINARY_DIR}" LEANC_CC "${LEANC_CC}")
Oh, that would make sense. It probably (still) works without the else because cmake ignores the missing variable?
